full_judgment:
5. The suit was contested by the defendant No.1 filing written statement. In the written statement it was averred that the suit was not maintainable, the suit is hit under Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and the plaintiff had filed a test suit having no real cause of action. The case of the defendant No.1, in short, is that before the CS record of right the suit land had gone into the water of the river and after 20 years the land was reformed-in-situ and as such under the provision of P.0.15 of 1972 and also under Section 86 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the suit land has been vested to the government as khas land. The plaintiff has no right, title and interest into the suit land and the suit is liable to be dismissed with costs. 

 7. The defendant No.1 against the said judgment of the trial Court preferred Title Appeal No.17 of 1992 in the Court of District Judge, Noakhali which has been ultimately heard by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Noakhali. During the pendency of the appeal in the appellate Court below one Mozibul Hoq son of Soleman was added as respondent No.2 in the appeal who filing a written statement in the appellate Court below averred that Tuka Mia while was -exercising his right, title and possession into 2.70 acres of land, the land was sold in auction and Sree Prosanna Kumar Das had purchased the land and the said sale was confirmed on 15.11.1924 and in the M.R. record of right the land was correctly recorded in his name in Khatian No.6 and 9. In the Diara settlement 2.24 acres of land out of the said 2.70 acres of land was wrongly recorded in the name of Kobbat Mia and others, the heirs of Tuka Mia. The remaining .46 acres of land was wrongly recorded in Plot No.40 in Khatian No.1 in the name of the government. 

 14. The suit was contested by the Government and Government filed a written statement and in the said written statement it has been asserted that the land had gone into the water and almost after 20 years the land was reformed in situ and by the operation of the law the land had vested to the Government. The case of the Government appears to be very much appetizing to hear but it is surprising to note here that the Government could not even state the name of the river where the land had allegedly drowned into the water. So how can the Government make his case believable that the land is the alluvial land? However, be that as it may the total scenario of the suit has been changed when the added respondent No.2 Mozibul Hoq made his appearance in the scene.
